findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — production unwrap on fallible I/O
findings.failure_mode: Any filesystem error (missing file, permission denied, ENOENT) panics the thread instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> and propagate with ? or map_err; never unwrap I/O in production code

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — production unwrap on fallible parse
findings.failure_mode: Any non-numeric or out-of-range value in the second CSV field panics the thread instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::Field(1, e)) and propagate; never unwrap parse in production code

findings.problem: Lossy as u16 cast from u32 without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: Values > 65535 silently truncate, violating data integrity; the function signature advertises u16 but silently corrupts larger inputs
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and propagate the TryFromError as a typed domain error

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: Empty line or line with no comma produces an empty parts vec; indexing [0] or [1] panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') and match on Some((name, value)) to handle missing/malformed fields gracefully

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: Line with only one comma-delimited field (or fewer) causes panic on parts[1]
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') and destructure into name/value bindings; never index split results

findings.problem: split(',') + collect() + indexing instead of split_once
findings.failure_mode: Allocates a Vec<String> for every line unnecessarily; O(n) per line where O(1) suffices; also enables the unchecked indexing violations above
findings.fix: Replace with let (name, value) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::MalformedLine)?; then trim and parse each binding

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — side-effecting I/O in data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: Hidden logging couples the core data-loading logic to stdout; makes testing brittle, leaks implementation details, and violates functional-core principle
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely; logging belongs in the imperative shell layer, not in the pure data-loading function

findings.failure_mode: Unbounded reallocations on large files; no bounded-allocation contract; allocation failure is silently absorbed by collect rather than being handled
findings.fix: Use try_reserve on the result Vec with a checked capacity estimate, or restructure to avoid intermediate Vec entirely

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<Record> with no bounded capacity handling for collection growth
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded file input can trigger repeated Vec reallocations; checked_add/checked_mul not used for any capacity computation
findings.fix: Pre-allocate with try_reserve using a line-count heuristic, or use checked arithmetic for any capacity computation

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string), side effects (println!), and data parsing in a single public function with no error model
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test the parsing logic independently from filesystem or stdout; any caller who wants pure parsing must refactor; violates functional-core imperative-shell split
findings.fix: Split into: (1) pure fn parse_line(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> for the core, (2) shell fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError> that handles I/O and delegates to parse_line

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 — no newtypes for domain values
findings.failure_mode: Any u16 can be assigned to value field; no domain invariant (e.g., value range) enforced at the type level; name has no format validation
findings.fix: Use newtypes like RecordName(String) with a fallible constructor, and use checked arithmetic or try_from for value to encode domain rules in the type system
